_description: Licence register of every text under static/corpus/original and every frequency list under static/corpus/frequency: what it is, where it comes from, its licence, the attribution it requires, and whether Ergopti ships its n-gram tables (status ship), waits for the maintainer (hold) or must not ship them (refused), with the evidence. The layout analysis codegen (tools/codegen/codegen-layout-analysis-data-js.cjs) reads the licence and attribution of a built-in corpus from here, refuses to build one whose status is not ship, and refuses a text with no entry here. Audit of 2026-11-14, decided by the agent, to review by the maintainer.

frequency/google_books/de_1grams_2020.js.title: Character, bigram and trigram counts and word table of the German words of Google Books, 1950-2019
frequency/google_books/de_1grams_2020.js.source: Google Books Ngram Viewer dataset, version 20200217, German 1-grams (ger, 8 shards), counted by tools/build/import-count-tables.cjs
frequency/google_books/de_1grams_2020.js.attribution: Google Books Ngram Viewer dataset, version 20200217 (Google, CC BY 3.0); J.-B. Michel et al., « Quantitative Analysis of Culture Using Millions of Digitized Books », Science 331 (2011)
frequency/google_books/de_1grams_2020.js.note: Licence read on the dataset page (fetched 2026-11-17): « This compilation is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported License », which allows sharing adapted material with attribution. Each 1-gram line gives a token and its match count per year; a token counts the sum of its matches from 1950 to 2019 (modern spelling, less OCR of old print), if that sum is at least min_count (100). Kept tokens are letters with inner or final apostrophes and hyphens: the part-of-speech tagged copies (« word_NOUN ») and tokens with digits or other signs are left out. A word list counted by the word-list rule: its n-grams are those inside words and at word boundaries, with capitals as printed but no punctuation or letter pairs across words. Its word table keeps the 1,000 most frequent words by the engine’s word rule. The 8 shards (6.2 GB) are streamed, never stored, each checked against its SHA-256 pin. N-grams rarer than prune_ratio of their table are dropped (pruned_below).

frequency/lexique/fr_lexique_4_10.json.title: Character, bigram and trigram counts and word table of the French word forms of Lexique 4.10
frequency/lexique/fr_lexique_4_10.json.attribution: Lexique 4 by B. New, C. Pallier, G. Schalchli, J. Bourgin and M. Gimenes (Behavior Research Methods, 2026), www.lexique.org (CC BY-SA 4.0)
frequency/lexique/fr_lexique_4_10.json.note: Licence read on www.lexique.org (« Lexique est distribuée sous une licence Creative Commons Attribution – Partage dans les mêmes conditions 4.0 ») and in the archive's README-Lexique.txt (« CC BY SA40.0 »), fetched 2026-11-15. Frequencies come from a 316-million-word subtitle corpus: spoken French. Each distinct form (1_Mot) counts once, weighted by the sum of its rows' frequencies per million (10_FreqMot, one row per lemma and part of speech) times 1,000, rounded; forms of weight 0 and the 290 multi-word rows (« citizen band ») are left out. The form total 11_FreqOrtho is not used: one form (« ben ») carries two different values of it. A word list: its n-grams are those inside words and at word boundaries, with no capitals, punctuation or letter pairs across words. Its word table keeps the 1,000 most frequent words of that list by the engine’s word rule (« aujourd’hui » counts as « aujourd » and « hui »). N-grams rarer than prune_ratio of their table are dropped (pruned_below).

Each self-dialog was typed by one crowdsourced worker playing both a customer and an assistant (ordering pizza or coffee, booking a ride, a table, movie tickets or a car repair), so the text is typed chat, typos included; the dialogs carry a meaningless id and no worker id, and names, places and orders are role-play. A scan on 2026-11-21 found 33 of the 169,469 utterances holding an e-mail address and 907 a phone number, a third of them visibly made up (« 555 »); they are counted like any text, and since only character counts and the 1,000 most frequent words ship, none can be read back from the table. Every utterance of self-dialogs.json is one line, counted as text (bigrams and trigrams cross words); the annotations are not read, and the spoken WOz dialogs are left out. English only: no French chat corpus with a free licence and no personal data was found (TODO.md). Only the counts and the 1,000 most frequent words ship, never an utterance; n-grams rarer than prune_ratio of their table are dropped (pruned_below).
